title: Environmental Factors and Career Adaptability: Effects of School Connectedness and Economic Constraints
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examined the interactive effects of economic resources and school connectedness on career adaptability, grounded in career construction theory and supplemented by conceptualizations from social cognitive career theory and the psychology of working theory. Participants were 3981 senior high school students from 91 high schools in Hong Kong. A latent moderated structural equation model was used to test the proposed framework. Findings revealed that school connectedness can compensate for the negative effects of resource limitations on career adaptability; however, its positive effects plateaued among participants with ample economic means. Furthermore, adaptability resources mediated the indirect, moderated effects of school connectedness on adapting responses. These results underscored the vital role that positive, relational school environments play in fostering career adaptability, particularly for students facing substantial economic constraints. Theoretical, practice, and research implications are discussed.
